title: A good generic lift in a prescribed Sylow quotient
statement: Let $e$ be a field [def-weil-field], $\ell$ a prime different from $\operatorname{char}(e)$, and $B$ a nonempty normal finite-type $e$-scheme that is a finite disjoint union of integral schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Let a finite group $G$ [def-sfb-finite-infinite-set] act on a normal Noetherian $e$-scheme $Y$ [def-pc-scheme] by $e$-automorphisms. Let $L\leq G$ have $\ell$-power order and index prime to $\ell$. Suppose $Z,Q$ are normal Noetherian $e$-schemes and $q_G:Y\to Z$ and $q_L:Y\to Q$ are invariant finite surjective morphisms for the respective $G$- and $L$-actions [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] [def-weil-surjective-morphism]. Assume their geometric fibres are the respective group orbits and their structure sheaves are the invariant direct images of $\mathcal O_Y$. Let $h:Y\to B$ be a $G$-invariant $e$-morphism and let $d_G:Z\to B$, $d_L:Q\to B$ be $e$-morphisms with $d_Gq_G=h=d_Lq_L$. Assume every generic point $\eta$ of $Y$ maps to a generic point of $B$ with $\kappa(\eta)/\kappa(h(\eta))$ finite [def-sc-generic-point] [def-weil-residue-field]. Suppose an open $U\subseteq B$ containing every generic point has $Z\times_B U\to U$ finite and a universal homeomorphism [def-weil-universal-homeomorphism]. Then for every generic point $b$ of $B$ there exists a generic point $c$ of $Q$ with $d_L(c)=b$ and $[\kappa(c):\kappa(b)]$ finite and prime to $\ell$ [def-pc-field-tower]. No condition is asserted for other generic points of $Q$. Normal means all local rings are integrally closed domains [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]; Noetherian means a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. No faithful action or generically free action is assumed.

Agent-extracted selection argument of returned item steps 7--9; localization of invariants: Stacks groupoids.tex Tag 03BK (lemma-invariants-base-change), part (3); inseparable degree: fields.tex Tag 09HI (lemma-finite-purely-inseparable).

proof.text: Fix a generic point $b$ of $B$ and put $k=\kappa(b)$. Set $Z_U=Z\times_B U$. By [def-weil-universal-homeomorphism], $Z_U\to U$ is a homeomorphism, and all its base changes are injective. Its unique point $z$ over $b$ is generic in $Z$: the homeomorphism makes it generic in a component of $Z_U$, and any irreducible closed subset of $Z$ properly containing its closure would meet $Z_U$ in a larger irreducible closed subset (a nonempty open in an irreducible space is dense), contradicting this maximality. By the universally-injective/radicial equivalence explicitly stated in [def-weil-radicial-morphism], $E=\kappa(z)$ is purely inseparable over $k$. Open restriction does not change these residue fields.

source.place: Tag 01S4, lemma-universally-injective; elementary generic-point argument for an open subspace

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-quotient-generic-fields] to $q_G$ with its given invariant sheaf and orbit-fibre hypotheses. Its component-orbit bijection supplies a generic point $\eta$ of $Y$ above $z$. Put $D=\{g\in G:g\eta=\eta\}$ and $M=\kappa(\eta)$. The same cited statement identifies the actual residue embedding $E\hookrightarrow M$ with $E=M^D$. Since $h(\eta)=d_G(z)=b$, the hypothesis on $h$ says that $M/k$ is finite. These embeddings are compatible with the base $k$ because $d_Gq_G=h$.

source.place: Tag 03BK, lemma-invariants-base-change (3), in the component-stabilizer form stated by the cited node

proof.text: Choose an $\ell$-Sylow subgroup $P\leq D$ by [lem-weil-pbc-sylow-subgroup-prime-index]. Regard $P$ as a subgroup of $G$. By [lem-sfb-sylow-conjugate-containment] choose $g\in G$ with $P\prime=gPg^{-1}\subseteq L$. Put $\eta\prime=g\eta$, $D\prime=gDg^{-1}$, and $S=D\prime\cap L$. The stabilizer of $\eta\prime$ in $G$ is $D\prime$: $a(g\eta)=g\eta$ is equivalent to $g^{-1}ag\in D$. Thus $P\prime\subseteq S\subseteq D\prime$.

source.place: X 2.3 Step 2, printed p.151, Sylow choice before diagram (2.c); component stabilizers of Step 3

proof.text: The subgroup $S\leq D\prime$ is an $\ell$-Sylow subgroup. Indeed conjugation gives a bijection $D/P\simeq D\prime/P\prime$, so $[D\prime:P\prime]$ is prime to $\ell$. The map of left-coset sets $D\prime/P\prime\to D\prime/S$ has every fibre bijective with $S/P\prime$, whence $[D\prime:P\prime]=[D\prime:S][S:P\prime]$ and $[D\prime:S]$ is prime to $\ell$. Likewise the fibres of $L\to L/S$ all have cardinality $|S|$, so $|S|$ divides $|L|$ and is an $\ell$-power. All the sets here are finite; these are just partitions into equal-size cosets.

source.place: Agent elementary finite-coset calculation expanding the Sylow selection in X 2.3 Step 2

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-quotient-generic-fields] to $q_G$ at $\eta\prime$ and to $q_L$ at $\eta\prime$. Since $q_G$ is invariant, $q_G(\eta\prime)=z$. Writing $M\prime=\kappa(\eta\prime)$ and $c=q_L(\eta\prime)$, the cited node says that $c$ is generic in $Q$, $E=(M\prime)^{D\prime}$, and $\kappa(c)=(M\prime)^S$, through the actual residue embeddings. Also $d_L(c)=h(\eta\prime)=h(\eta)=b$ by $G$-invariance. The hypothesis on $h$ gives finite $M\prime/k$; the action of $D\prime$ fixes $k$ since $h$ is invariant over $B$. The field $k$ is an extension of $e$, so its characteristic is that of $e$ and is different from $\ell$. Apply [lem-sfb-sylow-constants-field-degree] with base field $k$, field $M\prime$, group $D\prime$ and Sylow subgroup $S$ from step 4. Its purely inseparable fixed-field hypothesis is step 1. It gives $[(M\prime)^S:k]$ finite and prime to $\ell$, hence precisely $[\kappa(c):\kappa(b)]$ as required. This construction is made separately for each $b$ and makes no assertion about the other generic points of $Q$.
